claims.text: Al addition in CrFeCoNiX alloys preferentially promotes formation of an Al2O3 surface layer above 900 °C.
The Al2O3 layer is coherent with and adheres well to the CrFeCoNiAl substrate.
The Al2O3 layer grows slowly during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
A coherent, adherent Al2O3 layer resists cracking and spallation during prolonged exposure above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres.
The proposed initial CrFeCoNiAl alloy has a homogeneous elemental distribution in a single- or multiphase solid-solution state.
Good lattice matching and reduced thermal-expansion mismatch facilitate a coherent Al2O3/alloy interface.
At high temperature, Al selectively oxidizes relative to the other alloying elements.
Interfacial coherence reduces stress accumulation at the oxide/metal interface.
Reduced oxide/metal interfacial stress prevents scale cracking and spallation.
CrFeCoNiMn and CrFeCoNiSi form oxides with greater substrate mismatch than the oxide formed on CrFeCoNiAl.
The greater mismatch of Mn- or Si-containing oxides produces unstable scales.
After identical high-temperature exposure, CrFeCoNiAl will exhibit a more stable, continuous, and protective oxide scale than CrFeCoNiMn or CrFeCoNiSi.
The oxide scale on CrFeCoNiAl will show less cracking and spallation than scales on the Mn- and Si-containing comparator alloys.
A controlled comparison can be made among otherwise identical CrFeCoNiAl, CrFeCoNiMn, and CrFeCoNiSi alloys under the same exposure conditions.
Failure of CrFeCoNiAl to show significantly greater oxide coherence and adhesion and lower spallation than the Mn- and Si-containing alloys would falsify the proposed mechanism.
